what_its_for: BCG Live is used to treat early-stage bladder cancer that has not spread into the deeper muscle layers of the bladder. It is also used to help prevent bladder cancer from coming back after surgery. It works by stimulating your immune system to attack and destroy cancer cells in the bladder.
how_to_take: BCG Live is NOT taken by mouth or given as a regular injection. It is placed directly into your bladder through a thin, flexible tube called a catheter. A healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital will do this procedure for you. You will be asked to hold the medication in your bladder for up to 2 hours before urinating. During those 2 hours, try to change position every 15 to 30 minutes (lying on your back, stomach, and each side) so the medicine can reach all parts of the bladder. For 6 hours after treatment, urinate sitting down to reduce splashing. After urinating, pour 2 cups of undiluted household bleach into the toilet, let it sit for 15 minutes, and then flush. This helps safely deactivate the live bacteria in your urine.
dosing: The usual treatment starts with one dose given once a week for 6 weeks. After that, you may receive maintenance doses given less often, such as once a month for up to 1 to 2 years, depending on your doctor's plan. Your doctor will decide the exact schedule that is right for you.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule an appointment, contact your doctor or clinic right away. Do not try to double up on doses. It is important to stay as close to your treatment schedule as possible so the therapy works properly.
storage: This medication is stored and prepared by healthcare professionals in a clinical setting. You will not need to store it at home. The medication must be kept refrigerated between 35°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C) and must never be frozen. It should be used promptly once it is prepared.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive BCG Live if you have a urinary tract infection, blood in your urine, or if your bladder has been recently injured or irritated. Avoid having unprotected sexual intercourse for 48 hours after each treatment, as the live bacteria can be passed to a partner. Women should not become pregnant and men should avoid fathering a child during treatment — use effective contraception. Tell your doctor if you are taking antibiotics, as they can reduce how well BCG works. Avoid receiving other live vaccines without checking with your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: a fever over 101.3°F (38.5°C) lasting more than 2 days, severe or worsening burning or pain when urinating, blood in your urine that is heavy or does not go away, chills, flu-like symptoms that do not improve, joint pain or rash, cough or difficulty breathing, or signs of a serious infection anywhere in your body. These may be signs of a BCG infection that has spread beyond the bladder, which is rare but serious.
when_it_works: BCG Live begins working by activating your immune system shortly after each treatment. However, it may take several weeks to months of therapy before the full benefit is seen. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular follow-up exams and bladder checks (cystoscopy) to see how well the treatment is working.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you have HIV, are taking medications that suppress your immune system (such as steroids or chemotherapy), have a history of tuberculosis (TB), or have any active infection. BCG Live should generally not be used in people with a weakened immune system because the live bacteria could cause a serious infection. This medication is not typically used in children. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should not use BCG Live. Older adults can receive this therapy but should be monitored closely for side effects.
